- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.44) and price is rising, model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecasted peak.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.44) — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 75 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses early downward trends; if sentiment drops below 0.18 and price falls >1%, shift forecast 1–2% lower for next 2–3 days.
